newsitem.title: CANADA: MacMillan stock firms, aided by newsprint.
newsitem.headline: MacMillan stock firms, aided by newsprint.

text.p: Shares in MacMillan Bloedel Ltd were heavily traded and modestly higher Friday on stronger newsprint prices and continued expectations of a restructuring at the beleaguered forest products concern.

MacMillan shares were up 0.20 at 19.15 on volume of more than a million shares in Toronto. The stock has made similar moves in recent days in what analysts said was a recovery from lows hit earlier this month on earnings worries.
Analyst Sam Magid at Salman Partners said March industrywide newsprint price increases were a positive for MacMillan. "Finally a commodity is going their way," he said.
For months rumors have swirled that MacMillan will divest operations or take other steps to boost its share price as a way of appeasing disgruntled investors.

The paper division is considered likely to be the first to go, and traders have recently speculated that Fletcher Challenge Canada Ltd may be a potential buyer. MacMillan recently restructured the paper operation into a standalone unit.
A company spokesman reiterated on Friday that this step was intended to focus greater attention on the operation and not a prelude to a sale.

But analysts said the speculation has persisted and stronger newsprint prices were be a positive if the sale did proceed. "The paper division is likely to be sold and newsprint is its most valuable product," said Magid.
This has helped build expectations that if MacMillan sells the operation it may do so in a rising newsprint market and thus might generate a higher value.
Newsprint prices were raised US$75 a tonne on March 1. Analysts said the increase had not been fully implemented to all customers but that the benchmark price was now around US$575 a tonne.
